name: Stari Grad
tagline: The old town between the clock tower and the sea, all stairs
description: The historic core stacked on the slope above the water, entered through the Sahat Kula clock tower, with the Kanli Kula fortress above and the Forte Mare on the shore below. Squares, churches and stone lanes connected almost entirely by staircases rather than streets.
bestFor: Stays that want the old town and accept that everything involves stairs
pros: The most atmospheric part of the town
Cafes, squares and the fortresses all within a few minutes
Direct access down to the promenade
cons: Stairs everywhere, and a great many of them
No vehicle access and no parking

name: Setaliste Pet Danica
description: The paved promenade running the length of the town at sea level, past small beaches, swimming platforms and the marina, with apartment buildings and small hotels along it. It is the flattest part of Herceg Novi and the one place you can walk any distance without climbing.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to swim from the doorstep and avoid the stairs
pros: Seven kilometres of level seafront promenade
Swimming platforms and small beaches throughout
cons: The highest summer rents in town
Busy with walkers through the season

name: Igalo
tagline: The spa suburb west, with the mud baths and the flat ground
description: A separate settlement two kilometres west built around the Institute Simo Milosevic, a large therapeutic spa using the local mud, with a long beach, level streets and a mostly year-round population. It is cheaper and flatter than Herceg Novi and the promenade connects the two.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting flat ground, a beach and lower rents
pros: Flat streets, unusual on this coast
Long beach and the therapeutic spa
cons: Twenty minutes on foot to the old town

name: Savina and the Eastern Slopes
tagline: Around the monastery, quiet and green above the bay
description: The eastern side of town on the slope around the Savina monastery, with pine and cypress, quiet residential streets and views straight down the entrance to the Bay of Kotor. It is greener and calmer than the centre, ten to fifteen minutes' walk along the shore road.
bestFor: Quiet stays with views down the bay and the monastery grounds nearby
pros: Views over the bay mouth and Lustica opposite
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes to the town

name: Kumbor and Djenovici
tagline: The villages east along the shore towards Tivat
description: A string of small coastal settlements running east from the town towards Portonovi and eventually Tivat, with pebble beaches, small konobas and a much quieter pace. Rents drop noticeably as you move away from Herceg Novi and the bus along the shore road is frequent.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet shore village at lower cost
pros: Quiet pebble beaches and village konobas
Frequent buses along the coast road
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into Herceg Novi
Coast road traffic is heavy in summer
